title: FTC opens probe into AI giants including Anthropic and OpenAI | Reuters
content:
![The 'alarming' safety warning in the Anthropic IPO filing](https://ajo.prod.reuters.tv/api/v2/img/6abb8757e4b0326f6505aff3-1790692590196?width=1080&quality=80)

-   Summary
-   Companies

-   FTC to demand information from Anthropic, OpenAI and METR
-   Agency plans to compel executives to testify
-   Probe is Trump administration's first enforcement move on agentic hacks

Sept 30 (Reuters) - The Federal Trade Commission is conducting an industry-wide probe into Anthropic, OpenAI ‌and other AI labs to uncover the potential dangers their technology poses to consumers, a senior FTC official told Reuters on Wednesday.

The probe is the first official US enforcement action that delves into rogue AI agents, following a surge ​in incidents first reported in July that have stoked fears among the public that uncontrolled ​AI could one day harm humans.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

The FTC plans to issue formal demands for ⁠information and compel testimony from executives at top AI developers, including Anthropic, OpenAI and the research group ​METR, the official said.

Anthropic and OpenAI have used METR to conduct [independent investigations](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/anthropic-reports-fourth-cybersecurity-incident-with-early-version-claude-2026-09-09/) into security incidents involving their ​agentic AI technology.

Anthropic, OpenAI and METR did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters. The New York Post first reported the news.

FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson had concerns about the companies before AI agents developed by OpenAI hacked ​the open-source platform Hugging Face, the official said.

Item 1 of 2 OpenAI and Anthropic logos are seen in this illustration taken June 11, 2026. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration//File Photo

REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration//File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/illustration-shows-openai-and-anthropic-logos/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMlRSTEE2UFBUNA%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

But the incident in which OpenAI agents had probed ​the AI coding hub [for vulnerabilities](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/openais-rogue-agents-probed-hugging-face-weaknesses-two-months-before-major-hack-2026-09-16/) before carrying out a large-scale attack increased urgency around the issue, the official said.

Ferguson [suggested ‌last week](https://www.reuters.com/business/ftc-chair-pushes-back-treating-ai-agents-independent-actors-2026-09-25/) ⁠in an interview with Reuters that developers who instruct agents in cybersecurity tests that result in hacks should be liable for any harm they cause.

The US should look to existing laws before seeking to pass new ones regulating AI, Ferguson said at the [Reuters Momentum AI event, opens new tab](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gRS2saAYfug) in Austin.

The FTC has broad ​authority to sue companies ​over unfair or deceptive ⁠practices, and has used that authority in the past to take action against companies for failing to take reasonable measures to secure consumers' data.

US President ​Donald Trump [met with](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/trump-host-zuckerberg-anthropics-amodei-other-ai-titans-tuesday-2026-09-29/) top AI executives on Tuesday, where the companies agreed to ​establish voluntary ⁠standards.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

Trump has repeatedly called fears about AI a hoax as he seeks to prioritize US dominance in the technology over regulation. At the same time, he has also said the government can use existing laws against ⁠AI ​companies for any harm they may cause.

Anthropic said agentic AI ​technology raises significant and unpredictable legal risks in the prospectus for its stock market debut, Reuters [exclusively reported](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/anthropic-says-rogue-ai-agents-pose-uncertain-legal-risk-company-2026-09-29/) on Tuesday.
